report.summary: Detector fired on large SELL gross size with BUY fills (323, 67, 268) and cancels. The tape shows a two-sided PEGGED execution algo: 64 pegged orders, all children of parents P-T-X1006-05-B and P-T-X1006-05-S. It re-pegs BUY and SELL together as the touch moves (cancel symmetry 0.9998). Orders sit at the touch (0 ticks) at typical size 2586 (1.06x depth). The BUY fills were genuine executions on the resting orders, not an opposite-side benefit. The single SELL fill (624) came after the first cancel, with no favourable move or reversion. No spoofing feature is supported, so I propose closing as algorithmic re-pricing.

response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.80. It is a proposal only, awaiting a human decision (case C-A-261006-0008).

**The three facts that drove it:**
1. The orders are a two-sided pegged execution algo. All 64 orders are PEGGED children of parents P-T-X1006-05-B and P-T-X1006-05-S. BUY and SELL are re-pegged together as the touch moves, with cancel symmetry of 0.9998. They sit at the touch (0 ticks) at the desk's typical size of 2586, which is 1.06 times average depth.
2. The BUY fills (323, 67 and 268) were genuine executions on the resting orders. The one SELL fill (624) came after the first cancel. Price moved 2.5 ticks against the trader, with no reversion and no repetition in the session. Round-trip P&L was a marginal +0.51 ticks, which is consistent with spread capture. Neither of the two core spoofing features is supported.
3. No risk event or public market event explains the cancels. The trader has no registered market-making instruments and no prior alerts in 90 days. The desk's closed alerts on SYN.A were for a different trader and are context only.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the pegged children were not driven by their parents, or that the 624 SELL fill was obtained at a price the SELL-side orders had pushed. A longer frame showing repeated one-sided cycles would also change it. I only looked at the detector window plus 5 seconds of padding.

The first submission was rejected for a wrong field name in the report. I fixed it and resubmitted.
